Look. I'm not going to sit here and tell you with my metaphorical straight face and say I'm good at shooters. I'm not, never have been, never will be.

But I promise you, I am not exagerating nor driven by bitterness when I say that this game simply doesnt have a pitch for new players. None. Absolutely nothing. It genuinely doesn't matter what part of the game you end up touching, if it involves directly fighting another guy, and you are not a cut above the average FPS player?

You won't get rolled. You won't eat rocks. You will be brushed aside with zero effort. Fighting another player in a fair engagement literally feels impossible when you start out. 1v1, 2v2, 4v4, a huge blob at a choke, it doesn't matter. If you don't have someone absolutely pants down, dead to rights, you will lose the matchup a solid 80% of the time. That's not the worth part though, the worst part is the sheer amount of diving that you will have to deal with. Honest to god, I think I died to a light assault flanking me at least every minute. Didn't matter if I was alone or in a group, they are a constant, oppressive presence.

I played for a good hour or so. No tilt feeding, no rushing in alone. Purely by the books. I think I got like maybe 4 kills. 5 tops. I died at least 40 times. That's basically 1-10. For some perspective, even in really difficult tactical shooters like Rising Storm Vietnam, I only ever remember absolute lows of something like going 1-5,. Even then, that was rare, here it's just a regular occurance by all apperances. Seriously though, don't touch it with a 10 foot pole unless you're sure you're up for that. If you want big battles and cordination, you're better off just waiting for Foxhole to get it's ♥♥♥♥ together than wading into whatever this is.

Edit: Upon doing a little bit of searching, it seems that the game becomes relatively tolerable at low hours. I wasn't doing amazing there, but it was at least enough to somewhat enjoy the game.

claims.claim: The active player count has significantly declined, leading to fewer large-scale battles and struggles to find matches during off-peak hours.

citations.review_text:
Easy workaround for crashes:

[list]
    [*]Load into game
    [*]Immediately run to Warp terminal and warp to unlocked continent
    [*]Deploy anywhere into a vehicle and play as you wish
[/list]

Take too long at or between any of these steps and you will likely crash within 10 minutes. You don't need to waste time riding around at the home base, but some prefer to do so.

Check out SteamCharts for player count. As of writing, peak player count in the last 30 days was 700. My biggest gripe would be that you'll probably only play 2 or so different continents since games appear to take longer to end. I feel like I only play Amerish and Hossin in the evenings.

Not worth installing. The games claim to fame  is MASSIVE planet wide battles, and there's no other game that compares. The issue? You NEED a lot of active players (I'm talking tens of thousands for a game of this scale). The game has been neglected for years, due to it being F2P the cash shop took priority over core game play. The queue to even get into a game used to be larger than the games current active player count (about 400 on a good day). The only way out of the dark for this franchise is Planet Side 3, unfortunately unless someone else buys the IP the odds of that happening are non existent.

If you’ve never tried Planetside 2, it’s one of those games that’s hard to fully explain until you’ve dropped into your first massive battle. It’s a true large-scale FPS where hundreds of players fight across a persistent world. After 13 years of playing on and off, for me it still creates moments that no other game does.

The scale isn’t quite as wild as it was say 5-6 years ago —those organized formations and absolutely chaotic, screen-filling battles are a bit rare now—but don’t get the wrong idea. Big fights still happen, and when they do, they’re something special. Tanks rolling in formation, aircraft dueling overhead, infantry pushing through choke points—it can feel like a living battlefield.

That said, this game can be rough for new players. You will die a lot at first, and it might feel confusing or overwhelming. That’s normal. Planetside 2 isn’t about instant mastery—it’s about learning the flow of battles, figuring out your role, and gradually improving. Stick with it, ask questions, join a squad, and give yourself time to understand what’s going on before deciding if it’s for you.
If you’re willing to push past that early learning curve, you’ll find a game that offers something genuinely unique: unscripted, player-driven warfare on a massive scale. And when everything clicks, there’s nothing else quite like it. 

This game deserves glory. It’s currently on a downtrend, but I think with a light touch of care the new ownership, and devs can really make Planetside 2 be as big, if not bigger then before. Sky’s the limit here. It’s not gonna take moving mountains either.

citations.review_text:
TO PREVENT CRASHING THAT IS CURRENT HAPPENING IN THE GAME SPAWN A VEHICLE IN WARPGATE AND SIT ON IT FOR A FEW MINS THEN GO ABOUT YOUR GAMEPLAY FIXES THE CRASH ISSUE ANNOYING BUT IT WORKS.

I have both a love and hate relationship with this game, it's been a very long road from where it had started originally with many promises of features/maps which have never come to fruition, but the fact that it is still running after all these years and changing ownership many times. Whilst it is a shell of its former self population and server-wise, the game still has a beating heart, although smaller than it used to be.

This game excels once you are able to find yourself a group of like-minded people to play with, whether that is as infantry or in vehicle gameplay on the ground or in the sky. I'm not saying it's not fun for a solo, but it truly shines with some people to play with.

Infantry gameplay for me is, unfortunately, not where I find my enjoyment anymore, as over the years my home server Briggs closed due to reasons [downscaling of new owners/population], so I'm playing with a larger ping now on EU/US servers, and with client-side infantry gameplay, I end up dying a bunch when I'm behind cover, which can be frustrating. Although, admittedly, an essential part of the game for point defense and so on, infantry is the backbone of the game.

Vehicle gameplay, though, I feel is where this game shines for me — the driving force between bases and the air force to cover the skies and protect the little guys, flanking to take out targets, and the freedom of movement on the large maps between bases allows vehicle players so many possibilities and directions to do whatever they want, to have whatever impact they want on the battlefield. Nothing can prepare you for trying to defend a road between bases and 30+ vehicles coming rolling down the road with air support. It's just something you need to experience.

Air gameplay can be quite fun to learn but requires a whole heap of pa…

Been playing since release and there has still yet to be a game like planetside 2. I wish it were still popular but the early pay to win mechanics of the game I'm certain turned lots of players off right away. I understand the slow degrade. Throughout the years I have had very few crashes, some cheaters, but not too many.. less than other games for sure. I have spent very little money on this game and it has given me hours of enjoyment. In my opinion this is one of the best examples of a free steam game and a fantastic shooter. The learning curve is not steep by any means by today's standards, it's straight forward zerg faction battles. It's a great mix of Halo, Battlefield/COD, and some RPG if you want to go that route with farming and mining... I think competitive gaming has just taken too high of a priority over playing games with their intent in mind - to have fun. I would love to see a Planetside 3. 

Is it a good time to play? Sure. It's certainly a shadow of it's former glory, though. There is seriously nothing, and I mean NOTHING like having three 300-man battalions all fighting each other over one or two small territories (The Crown!)

Still no other game like it. If you like the idea of huge player driven battles involving infantry, armor, aircraft and even naval units this game is head and shoulders above anything else out there. There are a few notable bugs making it tricky when trying to log in which I imagine has turned away more than a few new players.

This game has many flaws, however, there is literally nothing like participating in the huge combined arms battles that only PlanetSide2 can generate.  I wholeheartedly recommend sinking a hundred hours into this game and seeing if it's something that speaks to you.

PlanetSide 1 was THE game of my childhood. Even now, years later, PlanetSide 2 still hits different. Whenever i have absolutely no idea what to play, i just install it and jump right back in. Sometimes i only last a single day, sometimes i sink two or three full weeks into it. The massive battles, the feeling of being part of something huge, the constant chaos, it is still unmatched.

Sure, it frustrates the hell out of me when it crashes right in the middle of a big fight or I get disconnected at the worst possible moment. And of course you cannot forget about all the cheaters and hackers that still roam the game. That is the main reason I eventually delete it again. But even with those problems, I cannot deny how much joy both PlanetSide 1 and 2 have given me over the last 20 years.

If you like big open-world FPS games with epic scale, this one is still worth your time... at least for a few hours until the frustration hits and you end up deleting it again. Thumbs up from me.

One of the best first person shooters, taking place on a massive scale I've never seen in any other game before or since. There are dozens of ways to play, from aircraft and tanks to infantry combat, and even base building. If you don't like one battle, there's usually 3 more going on elsewhere you can freely redeploy to, or even start your own. The social aspect takes things to a whole new level, with organized squads carrying entire battles. Given it's free to play, there's no excuse to miss out on this game.

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the game installs the BattlEye rootkit without clear notice on the store page.

citations.review_text: Every "Maintenance" update has significantly reduced the stability of this game. Reminds me of when devs break something just to say they fixed it later except these problems are growing. I shouldn't have to validate files, uninstall, validate files again, validate files in launcher, uninstall battle eye, redownload battle eye, and validate files every time I want to just login, then immediately crash when I get to the battlefield. Apparently you have to, once completing the previous steps, sit at warpgate for about 10 minutes before you can actually play. Mind you this process has had steps added at every patch since April '26. I dated it so I don't have to change it when I come back to update my  pre game play process because I would bet money this will continue to get worse. The game is great though. Also, I think its hilarious how many adverts there are for the Premium subscription and all I can think when I see them is "why would anyone pay for a game that is getting worse?". If you can actually login and stay logged in I really do enjoy this game.
sneaky bastards hide from the store page that this game installs the battle eye rootkit. I regret buying anything in-game.

citations.review_text:
TO PREVENT CRASHING THAT IS CURRENT HAPPENING IN THE GAME SPAWN A VEHICLE IN WARPGATE AND SIT ON IT FOR A FEW MINS THEN GO ABOUT YOUR GAMEPLAY FIXES THE CRASH ISSUE ANNOYING BUT IT WORKS.

I have both a love and hate relationship with this game, it's been a very long road from where it had started originally with many promises of features/maps which have never come to fruition, but the fact that it is still running after all these years and changing ownership many times. Whilst it is a shell of its former self population and server-wise, the game still has a beating heart, although smaller than it used to be.

This game excels once you are able to find yourself a group of like-minded people to play with, whether that is as infantry or in vehicle gameplay on the ground or in the sky. I'm not saying it's not fun for a solo, but it truly shines with some people to play with.

Infantry gameplay for me is, unfortunately, not where I find my enjoyment anymore, as over the years my home server Briggs closed due to reasons [downscaling of new owners/population], so I'm playing with a larger ping now on EU/US servers, and with client-side infantry gameplay, I end up dying a bunch when I'm behind cover, which can be frustrating. Although, admittedly, an essential part of the game for point defense and so on, infantry is the backbone of the game.

Vehicle gameplay, though, I feel is where this game shines for me — the driving force between bases and the air force to cover the skies and protect the little guys, flanking to take out targets, and the freedom of movement on the large maps between bases allows vehicle players so many possibilities and directions to do whatever they want, to have whatever impact they want on the battlefield. Nothing can prepare you for trying to defend a road between bases and 30+ vehicles coming rolling down the road with air support. It's just something you need to experience.

Air gameplay can be quite fun to learn but requires a whole heap of pa…

This is one of my favorite games of all time; however, it was ruined by constant crashing to the desktop after a couple of minutes of play. The crashing is widespread among many users, which has plummeted the already dwindling player count in the U.S. It has been months, and the crashing is still not fixed.

I've always loved this game.

It's a shame they can't keep the stupid crashes and other stuff from happening.

It's with a heavy heart I have to say this, but DO NOT play this game in 2026.

I've put hours into this game in the past. Had some of my better gaming memories forged in the fight for Auraxis. However something has gone very wrong rendering the game outright broken. Constant CTD with no warning. I can be trying to travel to a continent, I could be spawning a vehicle or I could just be sat doing nothing. Out of the blue and at random I will CTD. This is unacceptable, I don't care if you're no longer supporting the game. Take it off Steam if you're going to let it die. 

Years ago I would have given this game the highest rating and recommended it, but I'm sad to say I cannot do that anymore. Save yourself the hassle.
Love the game. But it crashes very often. Also getting server crashes. The game is not getting stable over the years.
The game is broken, it crashes all the time, and there is no future for it, it is a waste of time.

The game crashes literally 1 second after loading in on a fresh install

PlanetSide 1 was THE game of my childhood. Even now, years later, PlanetSide 2 still hits different. Whenever i have absolutely no idea what to play, i just install it and jump right back in. Sometimes i only last a single day, sometimes i sink two or three full weeks into it. The massive battles, the feeling of being part of something huge, the constant chaos, it is still unmatched.

Sure, it frustrates the hell out of me when it crashes right in the middle of a big fight or I get disconnected at the worst possible moment. And of course you cannot forget about all the cheaters and hackers that still roam the game. That is the main reason I eventually delete it again. But even with those problems, I cannot deny how much joy both PlanetSide 1 and 2 have given me over the last 20 years.

If you like big open-world FPS games with epic scale, this one is still worth your time... at least for a few hours until the frustration hits and you end up deleting it again. Thumbs up from me.

When it works its a fun game, especially for a FTP model. The problem is the frequency of game crashes makes it basically unplayable most of the time. This seems to be a common issue that so far isnt even acknowledged by the dev team.

Keeps crashing right after start up recently.
Paid for a membership for nothing and its non refundable.
Keep that in mind in case you wanna spend money on the game.
Now crashes in 1.34 seconds after loging in.

Game consistently crashes upon opening. Not able to play game at all. Cheaters in flying buses or people shooting thru walls, soft aimbot cheaters, all of it just make it not fun anymore. Fix the game please, nothing else is truly like this game and it is special to so many people.

I've been playing Planetside 2 for many years and after a short break I decided to come back. The game is total chaos, crashes and summoning a vehicle sometimes helps but I still have to admit that the fun is gone, what little there. I am done. I don't have the patience to support the game anymore.
Keeps crashing since lastest maintenance. Dont know why but yup.

citations.review_text:
WAY too many sus players, definitely plagued with hackers, "c" and "r" botters and hackers. everything you'd expect from a free to play / PAY TO WIN game. nothing redeeming about this game, after 800+ hours. its barely held together by tape and DayBreak cash. every element of the actual gameplay is unrewarding and stressful.

Gunfights feel completely lopsided, unless you're playing with any aim Bot or assist, you will lose every attempt at actually playing the game

you cannot hide, no matter the class spec or circumstance you will be found and you will be eliminated immediately no matter where or what you're doing, UNLESS you are 500+ meters away looking for nothing that exists because the hackers and bots cant see you.

vehicle combat its mediocre at best, the sweats and lvl 50+ will just farm you in to infinity, it takes way to long, and I mean YEARS not months to unlock everything. and you will be outmatched for months to years, which is the most unrewarding gameplay I've ever experienced. Well unless you use DayBreak cash, and pay literal THOUSANDS to unlock everything you will play unrewarded for maybe 3-5 years.

This is sellout PTW garbage, hackers go un punished, botters go un punished, and they will take your money for skins and armor that don't do anything, because no matter where you go the "c" and "r" will find you and ruin your gameplay.

I have played this game from beta and i can no longer support this game. The game is riddled with cheaters. People place spawn points underneath the map. Wall exploits to see people through walls. I can live with radar that goes over an entire region after maxing out scout radar on a vehicle, but radar doesn't spot you vertically. I can't tell you how many times I've been spotted from climbing over buildings or down tree tops. These people don't even have the sense to not blow up the only enemy spawn point when the number of players left playing this game at peak is what, 80 on a server? You end up running out of nanites and having to walk from the closest ally controlled region. This game is dead and it makes me sad. Don't bother giving them anymore money or time, find something else. I wish someone would make a Planetside 3 or equivalent game. I'm really going to miss how unique each of the classes are and the deep customization.
